RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the March 10, 2008/Phalguna 20, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Food Processing Industries; Human Resource Development; Law
and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable Energy; Power;
Social Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs; Women and Child
Development)
Total number of questions — 20
43
Compulsory registration of Hindu
marriages
*141. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE THAKUR:
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is considering
a proposal to make registration of Hindu
marriages compulsory under the law;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the reasons for bringing Hindu
marriages alone in the ambit of law, instead
of covering all the communities, uniformly
and simultaneously?
Reforming the educational system
†*142. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL : Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
educational system of the country is
not merit, excellence, research and
profession-oriented, as compared to global
standards;
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's approach in this regard;
(c) whether it is a fact that a radical
scheme is proposed to be implemented, to
bring about basic changes in the education
system of the country and to make higher
education knowledge and research-oriented
of international standards; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Scheme for adolescent girls
*143. SHRI B. J. PANDA : Will the
Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to launch a
new central scheme for adolescent girls, to
provide a package of compulsory services
to them;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether this scheme is proposed to
be implemented through Anganwadi
centres; and
(d) if so, the details thereof,  inter alia
indicating its action plan to implement this
project in Orissa?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

44
UN report on malnutrition and child
mortality
*144. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
  Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT  be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a UN report released says
that malnutrition and child mortality
continues to endanger the lives of children
in the country and accounts for 50 per cent
death of under five children and is also
responsible for the low weight among
children;
(b) whether, according to report the
country has to reach the Millennium
Development Goal of 38 by 2015, the
average annual rate of reduction in the next
nine years has to be about 7.6 per cent;
(c) if so, the other main points
mentioned in the UN report; and
(d) the steps being considered for
implementation of the report?
Violation of admission norms
†*145. SHRI UDAY PRATAP
SINGH: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn towards the violation of norms
for admission of children, by the private
schools; and
(b) if so, the names of the schools
against which complaints of irregularities
have been received and the action being
taken against those schools?
Power from Seepat Thermal Power
Project
†*146. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS :
SHRI BALA V ANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
 Will the Minister of POWER  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether an assurance of supplying
300 Megawatt in the first phase and
200 Megawatt in the second phase
from NTPC's Seepat Thermal Power
Project in the State had been given to
Chhattisgarh;
(b) if so, whether it was supplied;
and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Establishment of new IIT in
Gujarat
*147. SHRI VIJAYKUMAR
RUPANI: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Prime Minister has announced the
establishment of a new Indian Institute
of Technology (IIT) in Gujarat;
(b) whether there is also a proposal from
the Gujarat Government, requesting for
creation of a new IIT in the State; and
(c) if so, by when Government would
establish a new IIT in the State, considering
its highest industrial growth in the country,
that would serve potential research ground
for Indian students?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

45
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Maintenance and Welfare of Parents
and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
*148. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI :
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
 Will the Minister of SOCIAL
JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) which  States  have since given effect
to the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents
and Senior Citizens Act, 2007;
(b) the steps taken to give effect to this
Act with respect to the Union Territories;
and
(c) the number and percentage of senior
citizens who have been covered under the
Act, so far?
Approved Kendriya Vidyalayas
†*149. PROF. RAM DEO
BHANDARY  : Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) the details of Kendriya Vidyalayas
approved by Government in different
States of the country during the last three
years, including the present year,
year-wise;
(b) the details of functioning schools,
schools about to start functioning and post-
ponement of schemes due to any reason;
(c) the position regarding transfer of
approved schools to other States in case
the land and building is not provided by a
State Government;
(d) whether Government would
establish approved schools in the same
State for which these are approved; and
(e) if so, the details of action taken thereon?
Review of Protection of Women from
Domestic Violence Act
*150. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is setting up a panel to review the Protection
of Women from Domestic Violence Act,
2005; and
(b) if so, the reasons therefor?
National body to monitor quality of
education
*151. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the National Knowledge
Commission (NKC) has recommended the
creation of a national body to monitor the
quality of education in both Government
and private schools;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reaction of Government on the
recommendations of NKC;
(d) whether the quality of education in
Government and private schools throughout
the country is deteriorating day by day;
and
(e) if so, by when a national body would
be created to monitor the quality of
education?
Mahila Samakhya Programme
*152. SHRIMA TI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:

46
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
of United Kingdom has extended a helping
hand to Mahila Samakhya Programme,
which aims for empowerment of women in
rural areas for seven years;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that nearly
one million pounds would be given to our
country during the next three years, under
the above programme;
(d) if so, the details of assistance
extended to the rural women in Andhra
Pradesh; and
(e) to what extent this would help in
achieving the goal of sending every girl to
school by 2011?
Utilization of funds for women's
schemes in Uttar Pradesh
*153. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI: Will the Minister of WOMEN
AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
huge funds for women's schemes remain
unutilized in Uttar Pradesh;
(b) if so, the amount sanctioned to the
State for various women's schemes and the
status thereof;
(c) whether Government is also aware
that funds given for various projects and
programmes under the Protection of
Women from Domestic Violence Act in the
State also remain unutilized; and
(d) if so, what is the mechanism to
monitor proper utilization of the funds
allocated for particular projects?
Share of solar energy
*154. SHRI T.T.V . DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of NEW AND
RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the share of solar energy is
very nominal;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the action taken to increase the share
of solar energy?
Pending road accident cases
*155. SHRI HARISH RAW AT: Will the
Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of road accident cases
lying pending in various High Courts in the
country, as on the 30 October, 2007;
(b) the number of such cases lying
pending for more than ten years in
Allahabad High Court, as on that date; and
(c) what remedial steps are being taken
by Government to get these cases disposed
of, at the earliest?
Inclusion and deletion of castes in
SC list
*156. SHRI BALA V ANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) the procedure being followed by
Government to delete castes from the
existing list of Scheduled Castes (SC);
(b) whether any caste can be included
in the Scheduled Castes' list, without the
recommendation of the State Government;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) the number of cases pending for
inclusion of new castes into the list of
Scheduled Castes; and
(e) the time-frame fixed for taking a
decision in all these cases?

47
Underground cabling in Goa
*157. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
provide funds for underground cabling work
for power transmission in Goa;
(b) the towns proposed to be covered;
and
(c) the details of quantum of financial
aid likely to be made available to the State?
Curbing of capitation fee
*158. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has finalised
any legislation to curb the capitation fee
menace and also to bring transparency in
admissions in private professional colleges;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when it would be implemented?
Participation in Programme of
International Student
Assessment
*159. SHRI RAHUL BAJAJ:
SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state the reasons for not
participating in OECD's Programme of
International Student Assessment (PISA)
for assessment of science education quality,
while 67 countries, including developing
countries, do so?
Action plan for Remote Village
Electrification Project
*160. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of NEW AND
RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to
state:
(a) the action plan of Government to
help Orissa to light up remote inaccessible
villages in the State through non-
conventional energy sources,  i.e.  the
villages which cannot be served through
grid-power;
(b) the total number of villages in the
State that have been identified for
electrification under the Remote Village
Electrification Project (RVE); and
(c) the time-frame within which all such
villages would be lighted-up?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 4th March, 2008 Secretary-General.
Phalguna 14, 1929 (Saka)

159,
